newsitem.title: INDIA: High prices force India soybean units to cut output.
newsitem.headline: High prices force India soybean units to cut output.

text.p: Several Indian soybean processing plants have stopped production and some others were operating at lower capacities due to high soybean prices and restricted arrivals, traders and brokers said on Friday.
Traders said high prices were forcing soybean processors to buy less soybean.
"Due to heavy loss more than 60 percent plants have stopped their production and remaining are running at very low capacity," said Prakash Vohra, a soybean broker.
"Most of the plants are running at hardly 20 to 40 pct capacity and after a month they will switchover to rapeseed," said Gopal Agrawal, a soybean trader.
Industry officials say India's soybean output in 1996/97 (November-October) is expected to be around 3.5 million tonnes sharply lower than last year's 4.2 million.
"Soybean processors are making a loss of 500 to 700 rupees per tonne as soybean prices are high," said broker Dinesh Jadhav.
Soybean was currently quoted at 11,500-11,900 rupees per tonne in the central Indian markets compared to 9,500-9,800 per tonne at the same time last year.
Traders said daily soybean arrivals in the markets had shrunk to around 3,000 tonnes compared to 18,000 tonnes at the same time last year.

They said export demand for Indian soymeal was limited and prices were moving in a narrow range. Around 1.7 million tonnes of soymeal have been traded so far in 1996/97 (November-October), traders said.
Soymeal was quoted at $282-283 per tonne fas (free alongside ship) compared to $230 per tonne at the same time last year, traders said.
